messages:
Samir (Support): heads up — customer reports repeated CI deploy failures this morning. job runner hits 401/insufficient_scope when calling our Deploy API after token rotation. started ~08:12 UTC. logs attached below. any quick ideas? :eyes:

Anne (SRE): can you paste the exact error trace and which SA the CI is using? also which rotation/rotation-service did they enable?

Samir (Support): error snippet from the runner:```
HTTP 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"unauthorized","reason":"token_expired_or_insufficient_scope","detail":"serviceAccount:projects/12345/serviceAccounts/ci-runner@customer.iam.gserviceaccount.com"}
```
They say they enabled automatic key rotation for the SA via our managed-rotation addon. Runner is a self-hosted GitLab instance using short-lived tokens minted by our proxy.

Tyler (DevEx): quick checks: 1) token audience mismatch vs backend expecting `redwood-inference` audience, 2) rotation window produced a token that was not propagated to all runner pods due to a cache TTL on the proxy, 3) missing IAM binding causing insufficient_scope.

Anne (SRE): Samir — can you run this on the runner host and paste output?```
# show active token metadata
curl -sS --fail -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://metadata.server.internal/identity
```
Also check the rotation logs in the rotation-service:```
kubectl -n infra logs deployment/sa-rotation -c worker --since=30m | grep ci-runner
```

Samir (Support): ran both. rotation-service shows a burst of rotations at 08:10, 08:11, 08:12 with quick successive key versions. Proxy cache had entries for old token for ~5m. Runner curl returned:```
{"aud":"redwood-inference","exp":1670000000,"scope":"https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"}```
But our backend logs show it rejected because it expected scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform.readonly` (we recently tightened least-privilege).

Anne (SRE): ah — scope tightening + rapid rotation explains it. The rotated token had broader scope but the backend now enforces narrower scope, so token validation logic says insufficient_scope. Also propagation gap means some pods presented tokens with mismatched scopes.

Tyler (DevEx): mitigation steps: 1) temporarily relax scope check on backend for this customer to accept the broader scope OR 2) re-issue new tokens with the new narrower scope and force a proxy cache purge, OR 3) disable managed-rotation for that SA and perform a controlled rotation. Suggested immediate: purge proxy cache and redeploy runner pods to pick up fresh tokens.

Anne (SRE): for longer term: recommend switching to Workload Identity / OIDC where possible so runners don't rely on exported short-lived tokens + rotation race. Also tighten rotation-service to respect a grace window and propagate version info to proxy via a watches channel. Add leader election so rotations don't happen in parallel.

Samir (Support): did quick mitigation: purged proxy cache and redeployed one runner pod — deploy succeeded for that job. Customer asked for root cause summary and permanent fix.

Tyler (DevEx): file an action item: (1) update rotation-service to serialize rotations per-SA (2) add cache-invalidation webhook for the proxy (3) update docs to recommend Workload Identity for self-hosted runners. I'll open PRs.

deploy-bot: deployment/ci-runner redeploy triggered by @Samir — status: success :white_check_mark:

Samir (Support): thanks team. I'll send the customer a blameless summary: rapid concurrent rotations + cache TTL + scope enforcement mismatch. keeping this thread open until fixes are in flight.

Anne (SRE): noted. assign to Tyler for rotation-service changes. ping when PRs land and we can notify customer.
